newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Sterling takes limelight on Hungary FX futures.
newsitem.headline: Sterling takes limelight on Hungary FX futures.

text.p: Sterling attracted substantial speculative trade on Hungary's forex futures market as it's recent volatility on spot markets prompted short-term positions, traders said.
The pound accounted for half of all turnover on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) financial section, which saw a modest 3.93 billion forints turnover.
The Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) was tradeless.
"The pound's going up and down at the moment," said Gyorgy Varga, BCE trader with OTP Forex. "It's tempting people to grab it and liquidate their positions quickly."

Interest in sterling futures was spread across most maturities, with April rising one forint to 289.5 forints, June, the most active contract, was up 80 fillers to 296.30, and September up 93 fillers to 305.50.
All other turnover was in longer-term maturities of currencies which offer lower interest rates and could be used to speculate on the crawling peg devaluation of the forint.
Most notable was the March 1998 Swiss franc which rose 70 fillers to 141.00 forints.
The forint is devalued by 1.2 percent per month against a central bank currency basket made up 70 percent of the mark and 30 percent of the dollar. The rate will change to 1.1 percent from April 1.
Wednesday's central bank midday fix for sterling was up 1.36 to 287.99 forints, while the Swiss franc was up 0.33 at 121.15 forints and the dollar was fixed at 176.77 forints, down 0.49.
